The reverse side is a typical divided postcard back with address lines and a printed indication of rights and the year 1927 by the Budapest publisher Barasits.

A color postcard showing the front view of a large Romanesque-style cathedral with two tall square towers and a green roof, framed by trees and a landscaped park in the foreground. People are visible near the main entrance. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with address lines and stamp boxes, and printed information identifying the subject as the cathedral in Pécs, plus the photographer's credit.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a European city square with mid‑20th‑century cars. On the right stands a large domed former mosque with a cross on top and a spacious paved square in front, containing a tall Baroque plague column or monument with sculptures. On the left is a long, ornate classical building lining a tree‑planted street. The reverse side shows printed multilingual captions identifying the scene, handwritten Hungarian text, and a Hungarian postage stamp.

Black-and-white postcard showing a Romanesque cloister courtyard with stone arches in the foreground and the apse and tall bell tower of a large cathedral in the background. The reverse side is an unused divided-back postcard with Hungarian text identifying the location and the publisher.

The postcard shows a sepia-toned panoramic view over a historic European city filled with dense low-roofed houses and church towers. The photo is taken from an elevated hillside with rocky foreground. On the right side, a large crucifix with the figure of Jesus dominates the foreground, overlooking the city below. The back of the card has standard postcard layout with address lines, stamp boxes, and printed caption text in Hungarian and English.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a central square with a large domed church/mosque-like building featuring a cross-topped dome and an attached bell tower. In the foreground stands an ornate plague column or monument in the middle of the square, surrounded by steps and open space. Cars, horse-drawn carriages, and pedestrians line the adjacent street with multi‑story buildings on both sides. Hills rise in the background. Handwritten text at the bottom labels the scene, and the reverse side shows typical divided-back postcard layout with printed Hungarian text.

Color postcard showing the front view of a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall square towers and a row of arches and statues on the façade. In the foreground there is a plaza with flower beds and a central statue on a pedestal. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard layout with multilingual caption identifying the cathedral in Pécs, Hungary, plus printer and price information.

Colored vintage postcard showing an ornate Neo-Baroque theater building with multiple domes and elaborate sculptural decoration. The front top caption reads in Hungarian, and the back has handwritten Hungarian text, a green postage stamp, and typical postcard address and message layout.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a central square framed by an arch. Prominent is an ornate historic town hall with a tall clock tower and baroque details, facing a row of 2‑storey buildings and a busy street with pedestrians. At the bottom front side, Hungarian captions identify the scene as Pécs and Széchenyi Square with the town hall. The reverse side has handwritten correspondence, an address to Czechoslovakia, a Hungarian postage stamp and a small printer's mark from Budapest.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing the southern façade of a large Romanesque cathedral with four tall square towers and an open square with a central statue in the foreground. The reverse side has printed multilingual captions describing the view, handwritten Hungarian text, a Hungarian postage stamp, and postal markings.

A black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard with six photographs of landmarks and streets from the city of Pécs. The top left shows a large Romanesque‑style cathedral with four towers and a statue in front (Pécs Cathedral). Other views show civic buildings, a domed former mosque on a central square, a grand railway‑station‑like building, a clock‑tower on a street with a tram, and a square with a central statue and surrounding historic houses. The front caption, in Hungarian, reads "Üdvözlet Pécsről!" (Greetings from Pécs). The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, a Hungarian postage stamp labeled "Magyar Posta 40 f", and printed credits for the publisher in Budapest along with the words "Pécsi részletek."

Vintage sepia postcard showing a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall corner towers and an arcade façade. The church stands above a town with low houses and wooded hills in the background. Hungarian captions are printed below the image. The reverse side is blank with standard postcard address lines and a small printer's logo.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing an outdoor terrace café crowded with people sitting at tables, many playing chess or chatting, on a hill overlooking a sprawling town with low houses and, in the distance, a prominent church with twin towers. The reverse side has handwritten text in Hungarian, printed Hungarian captions, and a Hungarian postage stamp.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a scenic view over a city with a four‑towered Romanesque cathedral in the background. In the foreground, on a terrace framed by flowering tree branches, there are decorative stone balustrades covered with abundant fruit: a pile of large round fruits (likely peaches) on a tray atop a patterned cloth, and bunches of grapes arranged on a stone ornament. The reverse side is printed in multiple languages, identifying the cathedral in Pécs and laid out in the typical divided‑back postcard format.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large Romanesque cathedral with two tall western towers, viewed from across a series of cascading pools and fountains in a formal park. Trees frame the building and small figures walk on the steps leading up to the church. At the bottom of the image, printed captions in Hungarian read "Pécs" on the left and "Székesegyház" on the right. The reverse side contains handwritten Hungarian text in blue ink, address lines, a partial circular postmark, a missing stamp area, a small publisher logo reading "L. F. WEINSTOCK" and a printed serial number "3268/17. sz."

Color postcard showing a stylized street map of a city with Hungarian street names. Overlaid in the center is an illustration of a tall TV tower with red and white antenna segments and a circular observation/restaurant level. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with printed text indicating the location and publisher.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a landscaped park with tree‑lined paths and the stone remains of an old structure featuring large arches and walls. In the foreground a woman and a child walk along a curved path. The reverse side includes printed multilingual captions identifying the location as the Tettye ruins in Pécs, Hungary, along with handwritten Hungarian text, an address, and a Hungarian postage stamp.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard. The picture side shows a broad view of a hilly landscape with vineyards and terraces, with prominent stone ruins in the foreground and scattered buildings at the edges. At the top it is captioned in Hungarian "Pécs–Tettye" and "A fennsík teljes látképe". The reverse side has a green Hungarian stamp, dense handwritten text in Hungarian, and printed heading "LEVELEZŐ-LAP" with the address written to Budapest.

A color postcard showing a bright, sunny view of a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall towers and a greenish roof, fronted by an open square with flower beds, a statue on a pedestal, trees, benches, and surrounding historic buildings. The lower front margin bears the caption "PÉCS". The reverse side is mostly blank except for printed publisher information and the title of the scene.

Vintage colorized postcard showing a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall towers and a green roof, fronted by a circular garden and statue. The caption at the top left reads "PÉCS Székesegyház". The reverse side has handwritten text in Hungarian, address lines, and a circular postmark.

A black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard. The image side is divided into three vertical panels: on the left, a former mosque with a tall slender minaret and domed roof set among trees; in the center, a broad terraced garden with fountains leading up to a large Romanesque cathedral with four towers; on the right, a monumental statue of a standing man atop an ornate pedestal with seated figures around the base, located in an urban square. The message side shows handwritten Hungarian text, a green 40f Hungarian postage stamp labeled "MAGYAR POSTA" and "SIMONTORNYA", and an address in Budapest.

Two-sided vintage postcard. The front side is divided into four black‑and‑white photographs showing city views and religious interiors. The upper left image depicts a large square with the domed former mosque of Pasha Qasim in the center of Pécs. The upper right shows a panoramic view over the city with the four-towered Pécs Cathedral prominent on the skyline. The two lower images show interiors of a church or converted mosque with striped Moorish-style arches, an altar, pews, and religious decorations. The reverse side has Hungarian printed text, handwritten message and address, a green Hungarian postage stamp featuring the castle of Tata and marked "MAGYAR POSTA", plus a circular postmark.

A black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard. The front shows four photographs: a modern building complex on a forested hillside; a central city square with a large domed former mosque and an equestrian statue; a panoramic view over a hilly town with people sitting on a slope in the foreground; and a stone lookout platform with railings overlooking rolling hills. The back side has handwritten Hungarian text in blue ink, printed publisher information, a PÉCS postmark, and an address field.

A color multi-view postcard featuring landmarks of the city of Pécs. The front shows four images: a medieval stone fortification, the tall TV tower rising above trees, an ornate fountain in front of a large building, and a large panoramic view of the main square with a domed former mosque and surrounding historic buildings, statues, cars, and people. The word "PÉCS" is printed prominently in white on a black strip in the center. The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, a Hungarian postage stamp, postmarks from Pécs dated 30 May 1978, and printed publisher and price information.

A round multi-view color postcard bordered in orange, featuring four photographic scenes of the city of Pécs. The upper-left shows a historic cathedral with multiple towers above a hillside of houses. The upper-right shows a central square with a domed former mosque and surrounding buildings, cars, and a large paved plaza. The lower-left image shows a modern, terraced hotel or public building. The lower-right shows a broader cityscape with modern high‑rise blocks set against green hills. In the center front is a white label with bold black text reading "PÉCS". The reverse side has standard postcard layout printed in Hungarian, with areas for stamp, address lines, and price information.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall corner towers and an arcade façade, fronted by a statue in a circular park. Flanking the cathedral are historic buildings and tree-lined paths. Printed Hungarian captions read "Üdvözlet Pécsről" (Greetings from Pécs) and "Székesegyház" (Cathedral). The reverse side has the Hungarian heading "LEVELEZŐ-LAP", handwritten Hungarian text and address lines, a PÉCS postmark dated 1914, and a small printed publisher line at the bottom.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing the richly decorated interior of a large Catholic cathedral, focused on the high altar and ciborium with multiple steps, pulpits, arches and ornate ceiling. The reverse side has printed Hungarian text at the top and bottom and handwritten correspondence, address, and postmark.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a sloping walkway with trees and stairs leading down toward a small city. In the background, a large church with four Romanesque towers dominates the skyline, with hills visible beyond the town. The reverse side has Hungarian handwriting, a green Hungarian postage stamp, printed text indicating the view is of Pécs, and the recipient's address.

Colorized vintage postcard showing a lively European square with a domed former mosque and church tower on the left and an ornate multi‑story historicist building with shops and striped awnings on the right. A tram runs through the square among horse‑drawn carriages and pedestrians. The front is labeled in red with the place name and the square's name. The reverse side shows handwritten Hungarian text, address lines, and a purple Hungarian postage stamp denominated in korona.

A multi‑view color postcard with an orange border showing several scenes from the city of Pécs. The main images include a panoramic view of the city with a TV tower on the nearby hill, the central square with the mosque‑church with a large green dome and surrounding historic buildings, a view of the ornate City Hall, a pedestrian street lined with old houses, and a church with a tower and a small square in front. In the center there is a city emblem with a stylized bastion, red star and other symbols. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with address lines, stamp box, and Hungarian text indicating the publisher and photographer.

Round multi‑view color postcard with an orange background and four photographic views of a historic Hungarian city. The images show old fortress walls and towers, a large Romanesque cathedral with four towers, and a central square with historic buildings and a domed structure. In the middle is the city coat of arms featuring a stylized castle wall with a red star and an emblem below. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with address lines and stamp box, printed mostly in Hungarian.

A sepia-toned historic view of a broad European square with tree‑lined streets, horse‑drawn carriages and pedestrians. In the center stands an ornate Marian or Holy Trinity column on a stepped pedestal, surrounded by a low fence. Behind it rises a domed church with a tower and cross, flanked by long, classical multi‑story buildings. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard layout with address lines and stamp boxes, and printed captions identifying the scene and publisher.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a grand central square with historic buildings. A large eclectic-style city hall with a tall clock tower dominates the left side, while other multi‑story buildings and a church frame the square. People and shop awnings are visible around the plaza. The caption at the bottom of the image reads "Pécs" on the left and "Széchenyi tér" on the right. The reverse side has standard divided‑back postcard layout with Hungarian instructions about postage and the publisher's mark "Foto Weinstock".

Color-tinted postcard showing a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall corner towers and an arcade of arches along the façade. In front of the church is a circular lawn with a statue on a pedestal in the center and paths with benches around it. The caption at the top reads "Pécs. Székesegyház." The reverse side has printed Hungarian text indicating a correspondence card, handwritten message and address, a red Hungarian postage stamp, and postal marks.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall corner towers, fronted by a formal garden and statue. The building is set against low hills with surrounding city structures. The front bears printed Hungarian text "PÉCS" at the top left and "Székesegyház" at the top right. The reverse side has divided postcard layout lines, handwritten Hungarian address/message, a green Hungarian postage stamp, and a printed card number along the edge.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view over the city of Pécs from an elevated, tree‑framed vantage point. The foreground has a large tree and bushes, while the middle and background show dense rooftops, church towers, and the outline of Pécs Cathedral's towers on a hill. The back side is divided with Hungarian text, handwriting in pencil, a green Hungarian postage stamp, and a 1915 postmark.

Old black‑and‑white postcard showing a domed Ottoman‑style building with a tall, slender minaret rising in front of adjoining houses and a garden with benches in the foreground. In the upper part of the image there is red printed text reading "Pécs" on the left and "Török minaret" on the right. The reverse side has a divided back with printed Hungarian text, a circular postmark, handwritten message and address.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing the facade of a large Romanesque‑style cathedral with four tall towers and a central nave, seen from a square with steps, benches, trees, and a statue in front of the building. At the bottom front is the caption in Hungarian "Pécs, Székesegyház." The reverse side contains handwritten Hungarian notes dated 1935 Oct 6 and printed Hungarian text indicating rights reserved and the photographer/publisher in Pécs.

A multi-view color postcard with an orange border featuring landmarks of the city of Pécs. The front shows five photographs: a medieval stone castle or fortress; a domed church or former mosque illuminated at night; a tall television/radio tower on a hill; a modernist multi‑storey building labeled "Hotel Kikelet"; and an abstract modern sculpture on a pedestal in a green hillside setting. The word "PÉCS" is printed in bold black letters in the center. The reverse side is a typical divided postcard back with space for address and message, printed in Hungarian and another language, including a publisher line from Budapest and a printed price in forints.

A black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard featuring several landmarks of the city of Pécs. The front side shows six different photographs: an aerial view of a central square with a domed building; the richly decorated interior of a large church; a statue of a standing figure in a park; a round stone tower and old city wall; the façade of a four‑towered cathedral with a statue in front; and an ornate fountain or monument in a street scene. The word "PÉCS" is printed in bold capital letters in the center. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard back with address lines, stamp box, price, publisher, and the city name printed.

Multi-view color postcard with several landmarks of the city of Pécs. The central upper image shows the façade of a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four towers and a statue in front. Other views show an Ottoman-era mosque with a minaret, a medieval stone fortification with towers and garden, and a wide central square dominated by a domed former mosque, statues, busy streets, and surrounding historic buildings. The word "PÉCS" appears prominently in red on the front. The reverse has standard postcard layout with space for address and stamp, plus publisher information in Hungarian.

A multiview color postcard with a magenta background featuring five photographs of landmarks from the city of Pécs. The images include the exterior and interior of a large cathedral, ruins seen through an arched stone gate, a building complex on a wooded hillside, and a central square with a domed former mosque, a tall column, and an equestrian statue surrounded by parked vintage cars. The word "PÉCS" is printed in bold capital letters on the front. The reverse side contains Hungarian handwritten text, a Pécs postmark dated 1971, a red MAGYAR POSTA stamp, and printed publisher information in Hungarian.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large Romanesque cathedral with four towers rising above a tree‑filled square and surrounding buildings. At the front is a formal garden with paths and a statue. The caption at the bottom reads "Pécs" on the left and "Székesegyház" on the right. The reverse side has handwritten text in Hungarian, address lines, and a purple Hungarian stamp inscribed "MAGYAR KIR. POSTA" with a cancellation mark.

Multiview postcard with a brown border. The main image on the left shows an ornate stone fountain with sculpted animal heads and shields, standing in front of 19th‑century style buildings on a city street. On the right are three studio photographs of richly decorated ceramic pieces: a floral bowl with bright pink flowers on green legs, a tall two‑handled vase with intricate patterns, and a bulbous vessel with red and black floral motifs. The reverse side is a standard divided back with address lines, stamp boxes, and Hungarian text indicating the city Pécs and the Budapest publisher.

Colorized historic view of an ornate red-brick railway station building with towers and arched windows. In front are people with handcarts and horse-drawn vehicles on a wide square. Trees and a streetlamp stand to the left. The caption at the top reads in Hungarian about Pécs railway station. The reverse side is an unused divided-back postcard with Hungarian text "Levelezö-Lap" and a printed postage imprint for 10 fillér.

Color postcard showing a lush park scene framed by a large stone arch, likely a remnant of an old wall or aqueduct. Through the arch, a red gravel path leads toward a fountain surrounded by dense greenery and flowering bushes, with forested hills and a blue sky in the background. The reverse side is a classic divided-back postcard layout printed in Hungarian, with space for address and stamp.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view of a historic Central European city with hills in the background. In the middle distance stands a large church with four prominent Romanesque-style towers. In the foreground is a long, three‑storey school or institutional building facing a street. The reverse side is a divided-back postcard with Hungarian text printed on the left and along the center, plus a boxed note about postage in the upper right.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a grand Romanesque-style cathedral with two tall western towers and a long nave façade, viewed from across a series of terraced pools and fountains. People are gathered on the steps leading up to the church. Trees frame both sides of the scene. At the bottom front of the image the words "Pécs" and "Székesegyház" are printed. The reverse side is a standard divided-back postcard layout with Hungarian text about postage and a Budapest printer's mark.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a panoramic view of a large European public square lined with multi‑storey historic buildings, trees, pedestrians and horse‑drawn vehicles. The foreground includes a landscaped area and a monument. On the picture side, the captions read "Pécs" and "Széchenyi-tér". The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, an address, and an 8 fillér Hungarian postage stamp postmarked in Pécs. The card is printed with the publisher mark "Barasits Budapest".

A multi-view color postcard with an orange border showing landmarks of the city of Pécs. The front is divided into six photographs: an ornate historic building with a fountain, a city street with café terraces and red Coca‑Cola umbrellas, a large synagogue-like building, a tall baroque column in a square, the four-towered Romanesque cathedral, and a close-up of a decorative bronze ram's-head fountain spout. The word "PÉCS" appears prominently at the bottom. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with lines for address, a barcode, and the word "KÉPESLAP".

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a small domed building with a cross on top and, behind it, a slender turret-like minaret with windows and a pointed roof. Leafless trees and an iron fence stand in front of the structure, suggesting a winter or early-spring scene. The reverse side is a divided-back postcard layout with printed Hungarian text identifying the place and a date note from 1933.

A multi-view color postcard showing several landmarks and street scenes from the city of Pécs. The central images feature a main square with a column and statues, and a green-domed former mosque. Other panels show ornate historic buildings, a cathedral with twin towers, statues, and a tourist train. At the top right, large lettering spells out "PÉCS" next to a small outline map of Hungary filled with the national colors. The reverse side is a standard unused postcard layout with space for a message and address, plus publisher details.

A color postcard with a burgundy border showing the four towers and façade of a large Romanesque-style basilica rising above green trees and red rooftops. At the top, in an oval cartouche, is the name "PÉCS." The reverse side has standard postcard address lines, a barcode, publisher info, multilingual greeting, and a caption identifying the basilica and photographer.

Color postcard with two views of a historic Ottoman mosque and its tall slender minaret, surrounded by trees and adjacent buildings. The reverse side has multilingual printed captions identifying the site, along with standard postcard layout for address and stamp.

Color postcard showing two views of a large stone domed building on a square, with flowerbeds, benches, steps and parked 1960s-era cars. The structure is the former Gázi Kászim Pasha mosque in Széchenyi Square, Pécs. The back has multilingual captions identifying the place, standard postcard address lines, and credits.

Multi-view color postcard with five images of landmarks from a European city. The top left shows a charming pedestrian street lined with historic buildings, cafes, and outdoor seating. The top right depicts a large Romanesque cathedral with four towers and a statue in front. The center right shows a stone mosque-like building with a prominent green dome. The bottom left has a monumental fountain or statue group with a central standing figure and two seated figures. The bottom right shows an ornate baroque/neo-baroque theater or opera house with domes and decorative facades. The word "PÉCS" is printed in large green letters across the lower left image.

Multiview color postcard showing sights of the Hungarian city of Pécs. The upper images depict sections of medieval stone fortifications with round towers and an arched entrance. The lower left image shows the front of the Romanesque Pécs Cathedral with its four towers and a large statue standing in the square before it. The lower right image shows a full‑figure bronze statue of a man in a coat in a park setting. The reverse side has standard postcard address lines and Hungarian printing information, including the city name PÉCS and publisher details.

Multi‑view color postcard with an orange border featuring five photographs from Pécs: landscaped gardens with modern sculptures, a colorful geometric outdoor sculpture in front of a stone building, a tall TV/observation tower on a forested hill, and two modernist multi‑storey buildings surrounded by greenery. The back includes handwritten text, a Hungarian stamp showing fruit and labeled "MAGYAR POSTA 2 Ft", printed information in Hungarian, and address lines.

A multi-view color postcard with a blue border. The front features three main photographs and one small circular inset. The top image shows a modern terraced concrete building on a hillside. The middle image presents a central square with formal flower beds and paths; in the background stands a large stone building with a green dome (the former mosque in the main square), surrounded by historic facades and a statue. The bottom image shows a large modern housing or civic complex with white façades and multiple stories, set behind a landscaped park. The reverse side is a standard unused postcard layout with address lines and stamp boxes, printed text identifying the place and publisher details.

Color postcard showing a dramatic sunset behind four dark church towers with spires topped by crosses, framed by a thin border. The word "Pécs" appears at the top of the image. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with address lines on the right and printed information about the publisher at the bottom.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a busy central square with horse-drawn carriages, trees, and prominent historic buildings. A tall clock tower and ornate domed town hall dominate the skyline, with a column or monument and a church-like structure in the background. The caption at the bottom identifies the view as Pécs and Széchenyi Square with the Town Hall. The reverse side is blank, divided for address and message, with a small printer's mark.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a busy town square with horse‑drawn carriages, pedestrians, a central monument and surrounding multi‑storey buildings. Two church towers or clocktowers rise above the square. The caption at the bottom reads "Széchényi tér", and at the top right "Üdvözlet Pécsről". The reverse side bears the printed word "LEVELEZŐ-LAP" and address lines, with a blank stamp box.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a busy city square with a circular flowerbed and an ornate stone fountain in the foreground. People walk and cycle around the square, and buses are visible on the street. In the background stands a large domed building that was formerly a mosque, fronted by surrounding historic buildings with shops at street level. The reverse side has standard postcard address lines and printed Hungarian text indicating greetings from the city of Pécs.

Black-and-white postcard view of a central square with broad stone steps, flower beds and people sitting around. On the right stands a large, ornate multi‑storey hotel building with balconies and an inscription on the pediment reading "NÁDOR SZÁLLÓ" topped by a star. To the left is an older church-like building. The reverse side of the postcard has printed Hungarian text identifying the scene, space for a message and address, and an outlined box for a stamp.

A commercial postcard front showing a colorful historic square with ornate buildings, a tall clock tower, and a large baroque-style column monument with statues. The right half of the front is a grey design panel with printed text indicating it is a Pécs postcard collection by Ars Una Studio. The back side is a standard unused postcard layout with space for a message and address, marked with the city name Pécs and publisher details.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a central square with wide stone steps, low walls built of rough stone blocks, and a landscaped public area with benches and people sitting and walking. In the background stand several multi‑storey historic buildings with ornate façades; one has an inscription on its pediment and a five‑pointed star on top, indicating the socialist era. On the left edge part of an older church‑like building and a monument with a statue are visible. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard back with Hungarian text identifying the view and the publisher, plus a printed price.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall towers and an arcaded façade, set in a town with hills in the background. Handwritten-style caption at the bottom reads "Pécs-Székesegyház." The reverse side is a typical divided-back postcard layout with Hungarian text indicating rights reserved and the publisher's details.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing the richly decorated interior of a large cathedral with vaulted ceilings, ornate arches, frescoes, and an elaborate high altar approached by several stairways. At the bottom left of the front image is a printed caption. The reverse side shows typical postcard layout with Hungarian text, a Hungarian stamp, postmark, address lines, and handwritten message.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing stone ruins on a hill surrounded by vegetation, with two small human figures near an arched opening. The front caption at the bottom reads "Pécs" on the left and "Tettyei romok" on the right. The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, an address, and a magenta Hungarian postage stamp marked "MAGYARORSZÁG 8 FILLÉR", with a circular postmark from Pécs dated November 24, 1928. Printer information "Barasits Budapest" and a copyright line with the year 1927 appear at the bottom.

A multi-view color postcard featuring various landmarks and street scenes from the city of Pécs. The front shows a collage: a road with a railing and the towers of a cathedral in the distance, historic buildings around a central monument in a square, garden views with sculptures and the façade of a cathedral, an Ottoman-era mosque with a green dome, outdoor cafés, and a decorative close-up detail. At the top is the word 'PÉCS' over a tricolor background resembling the Hungarian flag and the outline map of Hungary. The back is a standard unused postcard layout with a vertical publisher imprint and a barcode.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard. The front shows a panoramic view over the historic center of Pécs framed by tree branches, with church towers and a dome rising above old city walls and rooftops; hills and fields appear in the distance. At the bottom of the image there is a Hungarian caption printed in white. The reverse side has a green Hungarian postage stamp, circular postmark, printed address lines, a typed address to Dr. Fábry Lajos in Budapest, and a handwritten Hungarian message.

A sepia-toned historic street scene showing a large ornate late‑19th‑century bank or savings building on a city square, with horse‑drawn carriages, pedestrians, trees, and a sculpted column or monument in the foreground. The façade of the main building bears Hungarian inscriptions, and printed captions at the bottom identify the location and the institution. The reverse side is a blank divided-back postcard with Hungarian text for 'postcard' and the publisher's line along the left edge.

Color postcard showing an ornate stone fountain with a tall, richly decorated central pillar topped by a small roof-like structure. Around the base are four bronze animal heads (likely oxen) spouting water into a circular basin. The fountain stands in a flower bed in front of a historic building with arched windows and doorways. The reverse side has Hungarian handwriting, an orange Hungarian postage stamp, and printed caption information along the edge.

Color postcard showing a busy central square with a decorative Zsolnay fountain in the foreground, featuring ornate ceramic details and animal heads. Surrounding it are flower beds, 1960s-era cars, buses, and pedestrians. In the background stands a domed former mosque on a hill-facing square with additional statues and buildings. The reverse side has Hungarian handwriting, a red Hungarian stamp, and printed captions indicating the subject of the card.

Black-and-white historic postcard showing an ornate multi-storey neo-baroque/neo-renaissance bank building on a large square with people walking, a horse-drawn cart, and a monumental fountain or statue group in the foreground. Hungarian text is printed below the image and along the left edge, identifying the scene as the savings bank palace in Pécs.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a grand historic city hall building with a tall clock tower dominating a public square filled with horse‑drawn carriages and people. Smaller buildings and a church‑like structure frame the square. The front has the printed captions "Pécs" at the upper left and "Városháza" at the upper right. The reverse side is a standard divided‑back postcard layout with vertical Hungarian text along the left indicating a Budapest publisher and a small boxed logo with the letters "K. R." near the bottom.

Multi-view black-and-white postcard showing several landmarks of a city: a large Romanesque cathedral with four towers and a terraced fountain in front, panoramic views over a hilly city with a prominent cross on a rocky outcrop, modern public buildings and squares, a curving road around a hillside complex, a lookout tower in a wooded area, a decorative urn in a park, and a large outdoor swimming pool. At the bottom front, Hungarian text reads "ÜDVÖZLET PÉCSRŐL." The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text in red ink, a Hungarian stamp, postmark, and printed publisher details.

Colorized view of stone ruins standing alone in an open grassy park, with a curving dirt path in the foreground. Trees and a few hillside houses appear in the background, along with a small pavilion-like building to the right. The reverse side has printed Hungarian text indicating the location and publisher, laid out in the typical divided-back postcard format.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a grand brick railway station complex with ornate facades, arched windows, and a central entrance pavilion topped by steep roofs and small towers. The words "Pécs" and "Indóház" are printed on the image side. The reverse side has Hungarian handwritten text, a green postage stamp labeled "MAGYAR KIR. POSTA 5 FILLER," postmarks, and the printed heading "LEVELEZŐ-LAP."

Colorized historic postcard showing a central square with a grand town hall building featuring a tall clock tower and green roof, a baroque column or monument in the foreground with horse‑drawn carriages around it, and other surrounding buildings and trees. The caption beneath the image reads in Hungarian. The reverse side is blank with standard postcard dividing line and address lines.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view of the city of Pécs with hills in the background and an open field with a few people in the foreground. Prominent church towers rise above the cityscape. At the top it is captioned in Hungarian and German. The lower front margin bears a handwritten greeting and signature. The reverse side is printed as a correspondence card in Hungarian and addressed in elegant cursive handwriting, with a postmark from Pécs and a postage stamp.

A vintage color aerial view of a densely built historic city center with red‑tiled roofs, narrow streets and several prominent public buildings and squares. The reverse side is a divided‑back postcard with multilingual caption and Hungarian publisher information, price and photo credit.

Color postcard with a burgundy frame showing a statue in front of a large Romanesque-style cathedral with multiple towers and arched windows, bordered by a flowerbed of red tulips under a blue sky. The word "PÉCS" is printed prominently on the front. The reverse side has space for address and stamp, multilingual greetings from Pécs, a barcode, publisher information, and the word "Bazilika".

Vintage color postcard showing stone ruins with a large arched opening and fragmented walls set on a grassy area with tall trees and hills in the background. Several men in early-20th‑century attire stand near the arch. The back side has handwritten text in Hungarian, postal markings, and space for the address. The front caption at the bottom identifies the location as Pécs‑Tettye and mentions details of the ruins.

A vintage sepia-toned postcard. The front shows a panoramic view of a hilly, wooded area with a winding road, scattered houses and tall trees. In the foreground are prominent stone ruins on an open plateau. At the bottom margin, Hungarian text identifies the location as part of the Mecsek hills near Pécs. The reverse side contains a handwritten Hungarian message, an address in Budapest, a printed Hungarian postage instruction box, and a circular postal cancellation mark.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view over the rooftops of a town toward a large Romanesque cathedral with four tall square towers. Vegetation frames the foreground, while the city and distant landscape stretch into the haze. The caption at the bottom front identifies the view and city in Hungarian. The reverse side is an unused divided‑back postcard printed in Hungarian, with space for address and stamp and a small printer's mark from Budapest.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a busy central square with a large ornate fountain in the middle, surrounded by crowds of people in early 20th‑century clothing, horse‑drawn carriages and a tram. Multi‑story historic buildings with shops and awnings line the square. The captions at the bottom identify the place as Pécs and the square as Széchenyi tér. The reverse side is blank with the usual divided‑back layout for address and message, and a small publisher's logo at the bottom.

Vintage sepia postcard showing an ornate historic theatre building with domes and rich Neo-Baroque decoration. The structure has a large central dome, side domes, grand staircases, arched windows and classical columns on the façade. At the bottom margin of the image, Hungarian text identifies the location and building.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a broad public square with a large Baroque-style plague column or fountain in the center and an ornate historic town hall building with a clock tower on the right. Several pedestrians stand in the open square. The front bottom margin carries handwritten-style captions that read "Pécs" on the left and "Városháza" on the right. The reverse side is a classic divided postcard back with address lines and stamp box, printed with publisher information in Hungarian.

The postcard's front shows an old black‑and‑white photograph of a broad European square bordered by multi‑storey classical buildings. In the center right stands an ornate Baroque column with statues and a sunburst at the top, surrounded by a low fence and steps. Behind it is a large church with a domed roof and a tall, slender bell tower. Horse‑drawn carriages and a few pedestrians occupy the largely unpaved square, with trees and benches scattered around. The reverse side is a standard modern postcard layout, with printed lines for the address and stamp, and printed text identifying the place and publisher.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a domed building with a cross on top and an adjacent slender Ottoman‑style minaret rising above trees and nearby houses. The front caption at the bottom reads "Pécs. Török minaret." The reverse side has handwritten text in blue ink in Hungarian, a Hungarian postage stamp, and postal cancellations.

A vintage black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard. The front is divided into nine small photographs showing various sights of a city: a skyline with a large four‑towered cathedral, civic and university‑style buildings, a church with a tall clock tower, a landscaped lake or pond, a busy swimming pool or bathing beach, hillside buildings, a modernist complex with a tall mast or monument, and a central square with a fountain and a statue. The back has standard postcard layout with space for message, address lines, a dotted stamp box, and printed Hungarian text and publisher's mark.

A vintage divided-back postcard. The front shows a colorized street scene with several multi‑storey buildings and horse‑drawn carriages in front. The central building is labeled as the Nádor Hotel. Bare trees line the wide street. On the message side, there is printed Hungarian text "Levelező-Lap" and a Budapest postmark dated August 20, 1908, along with handwritten Hungarian correspondence and address details.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a large historic building complex with an ornate façade and a tall clock/bell tower on a city square. The building has Baroque and eclectic architectural details and houses street-level shops. In the upper left corner the printed word "Városház." appears, and in the upper right corner "Pécs." The reverse side shows handwritten Hungarian text, a green Hungarian postage stamp, postmarks, and the printed heading "LEVELEZŐ LAP" along with a publisher line at the bottom.

A vintage multi-view postcard with a dark border and a central scroll bearing a greeting in Hungarian, surrounded by small black-and-white photographs of notable sites in and around the city of Pécs. Each vignette is captioned in Hungarian, showing buildings such as a mausoleum, hotel, theater, school, church, city square, Roman ruins, and villa-lined street. The reverse side has the typical divided-back layout with the printed word 'Levelező-lap', handwritten cursive message and address lines, and a green Hungarian postage stamp canceled with a PÉCS postmark.

Color postcard showing a panoramic view of a central square in a historic European city. In the foreground is a large paved square with a column-like monument. On the right stands a distinctive historic building with a large blue-green dome – a former mosque – surrounded by a curved street lined with parked cars from the late 20th century. On the left is a long Baroque-style building with a red-tiled roof, and in the distance a cathedral with four tall towers is visible above the rooftops. The lower border of the card bears the word "PÉCS" in large serif letters. The reverse side is a standard unused postcard layout with address lines, stamp boxes and publisher information.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a lively street scene in a historic European city. On the right are ornate multi‑storey buildings with elaborate facades; at the end of the street stands a large domed building in a square, with hills visible in the distance. People, buses and a tram are in the foreground, suggesting an active urban centre. Below the image is the printed caption in Hungarian, and the reverse side has a Hungarian postage stamp, postmark, printed publisher information, and handwritten Hungarian text and address lines.

Illustrated postcard showing the skyline of Strasbourg with the tall Gothic spire of Strasbourg Cathedral rising above the city. To the right, large white storks fly across the sky carrying French tricolor flags with golden fringes and symbols, evoking liberation or national celebration. The dates 1870 and 1918 flank the cathedral, and the word 'Strasbourg' appears in decorative script. A small artist signature is at the lower right.

Monochrome postcard showing a grand military parade passing in front of an ornate neo‑Renaissance stone building. Cavalry officers ride horses along a broad avenue while large crowds of civilians and soldiers watch from the street, the steps, balconies, and windows of the building. The façade features rusticated stonework, arched windows, heavy balustrades, and large sculpted atlantes supporting the balcony. The image is bordered below by a tonal scale and measurement marks, suggesting this is a reproduction of an old postcard.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large military parade passing in front of an ornate neo‑Renaissance stone building. Infantry soldiers wearing early 20th‑century uniforms and helmets march with rifles, while a mounted officer on horseback rides at the front. A dense crowd of civilians watches from the street and from balconies and windows of the grand façade behind them, which features arched windows, heavy rustication, sculpted figures and balustraded balconies. The overall impression is of a ceremonial review or victory parade in a European city.

A black‑and‑white wartime postcard showing American soldiers marching in formation through a large Parisian square, rifles on their shoulders and a U.S. flag at the front. In the background stands a monumental statue on a pedestal, surrounded by a grand neoclassical building with columns and arched ground floor, likely the Place de la Concorde area. The postcard includes bilingual French and English captions beneath the image, identifying the scene as an American troops parade before the Statue of Strasbourg in Paris on July 4th, 1918.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a central town hall building with a high clock tower topped by a bulbous dome and small lantern. The ground floor has shops and arcades, with a horse‑drawn cart and several pedestrians in the square in front. Printed captions in three languages at the bottom identify the building and town; handwritten message in ink covers part of the lower margin. The reverse side has the typical divided postcard layout with Hungarian text "LEVELEZŐ-LAP", address written in cursive, postage stamps and postmarks.

Sepia-toned historical postcard showing a busy central square with many horse-drawn carriages and pedestrians. On the left dominates a large Gothic church with buttresses and a high roof; in front and to the right are multi-story townhouses with shops at street level bearing German-language signs. The reverse side has a divided back with printed trilingual heading "Brașov—Kronstadt—Brassó" and the publisher credit "Verlag H. Zeidner."

Colorized historic postcard showing the massive round White Tower (Turnul Alb) of Brașov with crenellated walls and a small red‑roofed annex. In the foreground, people in early‑20th‑century clothing stroll and sit on benches along a tree‑lined promenade; in the background appears part of the town and surrounding hills. The front caption names Brașov and the tower in multiple languages (Romanian, Hungarian, German). The reverse bears the bilingual heading for postcard/cardă poștală in Romanian and Hungarian.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a statue of a robed man standing on a pedestal in front of a large Gothic stone church wall with arched windows. Low railings and shrubs surround the monument. The front caption indicates it is the Honterus monument in Kronstadt (Brasov). The reverse is largely blank with a vertical publisher's imprint in German.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a cobblestone street lined with historic multi‑story buildings, shop signs and pedestrians with a cart in the foreground. At the end of the street rise two tall church towers. The caption at the top lists the city name in several languages and identifies the street. The reverse has typical postcard dividing lines and the Hungarian phrase 'LEVELEZŐ-LAP'.

Colorized street view of a grand boulevard lined with stately 19th‑century buildings and trees, with hills in the background. A prominent stone mansion with ornate façade and balcony stands on the right behind an iron fence. Pedestrians walk along the wide unpaved road. The front text at the top reads in German and Hungarian: "Kronstadt. — Brassó." and on the right "Rudolfring. — Rezső-körút." The reverse side shows handwritten correspondence in German, Hungarian postal markings and the Hungarian word for postcard "Levelező lap", addressed to Frl. Mausi Stenzel in Hermannstadt, Siebenbürgen.

Colorized panoramic view of a historic town nestled in a valley surrounded by green mountains. The town has dense blocks of buildings with red roofs and several prominent church towers and large public buildings. The caption at the top identifies the view in Hungarian and German. The reverse side shows a divided back with Hungarian text layout and a small crest or emblem.

Old color-printed postcard with two architectural views of a historic town hall complex. The left vignette, titled "Eingang zum Rathaus.", shows people walking through an arched gateway leading into a courtyard surrounded by buildings with red-tiled roofs. The right vignette, titled "Rathausshof", depicts the inner courtyard of the same town hall, with ivy-covered walls, wooden balconies, and a tall corner tower. At upper right is printed the greeting "Gruss aus Hermannstadt." in red. The front is densely covered with handwritten script in German. The reverse side is a divided postcard back printed with the Hungarian word "LEVELEZŐ-LAP.", address lines filled in cursive, a postal cancellation, and Hungarian stamps.

A colorized postcard view of a historic European town square surrounded by red‑roofed buildings. The square is busy with people, horse‑drawn carts, trees, market stalls and parasols. On the right rises a large clock tower overlooking the rooftops, with hills visible in the distant background. The caption at the top names the city in three languages and identifies the square. The reverse side is a standard divided-back layout labeled as a Romanian postcard, with printer information at the bottom.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph showing a city street with a central fountain in the foreground and historic multi‑story buildings lining the street. A tall baroque church tower with a clock dominates the right side. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk along the street and around the square. Printed caption text at the top left reads "Graz. Herrengasse".

Vintage monochrome postcard showing the Kasr El Nil Bridge in Cairo. At the entrance to the bridge stand two large lion statues on pedestals. People in traditional clothing and a camel are in the foreground, with the bridge and lampposts stretching into the distance. The title is printed at the top, and a website watermark appears at the bottom right.

Sepia-toned postcard showing an elevated view of a grand semicircular colonnade enclosing an open square. People are strolling in the plaza, which is surrounded by elegant classical buildings. Forested hills appear in the distant background. French caption text is printed along the bottom margin.

Black‑and‑white view down a cobblestone street in a historic European town, lined with two‑ and three‑story stucco or stone houses with steep tiled roofs. People in early 20th‑century clothing (men in suits, women in long dresses and aprons, children in caps and coats) stand and walk along the street. In the distance a tall church or town‑hall tower with a spire dominates the skyline. Hanging signs identify a restaurant and café on the right side.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view of a small European town on a hill, with open fields in the foreground and a winding path leading toward the settlement. The town features clustered houses with pitched roofs and a prominent church with a tall tower and spire dominating the skyline. Trees and hillside vegetation surround the built-up area. The town name "Dohna." is printed in red at the bottom, and a publisher's line appears along the lower edge. A red handwritten number "2281" is written in the upper right corner.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a monumental architectural gateway with a very large central arch flanked by engaged columns and blind arcades. The façade is heavily stylized, with multiple rectangular window-like recesses above, decorative friezes, and smaller arched niches below. The scene appears to be indoors, possibly a museum gallery, with stone slabs or sculptures visible through the dark opening behind the arch. There is a wide, empty floor area in the foreground and no visible people or text on the image.

A colorized historic postcard view of Cairo's Citadel complex. In the foreground are stone fortification towers, people walking, horse-drawn carriages, and soldiers or guards in red uniforms. In the background, a large mosque with a central dome and two tall minarets dominates the skyline, likely the Mosque of Muhammad Ali within the Cairo Citadel. The style is early 20th‑century chromolithograph.

A black-and-white postcard view of historic brick houses along a canal, with gabled roofs and a small arched bridge reflected in the water. A rowboat with a person is visible on the left. Large trees frame the canal, and church spires rise in the distant background. Printed captions at the bottom identify the scene as old houses on the Rosary Quay in Bruges.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a historic multi‑storey palace-like building with ornate gables and towers, partly obscured by tall trees and landscaped park grounds. A path curves through the grass in the foreground. Printed caption text appears along the bottom margin.

A vintage, blue-tinted postcard view over a harbor area with several passenger boats and smaller vessels docked along the quay. In the background are tree-lined streets, a busy square with horse‑drawn carriages and early automobiles, and large ornate stone buildings. A prominent building with a grand façade and columned entrance is visible to the right; this is the Dramaten (Royal Dramatic Theatre). The caption at the bottom identifies the scene as Stockholm's Nybroplan with the Dramatiska Teatern.

Black‑and‑white image of a European old town street dominated by a tall church tower with a very slender, steep spire. The tower has a square base with arched windows and belfry openings, and it is flanked by narrow historic townhouses with steep, tiled roofs lining a cobbled street. Trees are visible on the left side and a few early‑20th‑century cars are parked along the street. There is no visible printed caption on the image side.

A colorized vintage coastal view showing a fortified historic town by the sea, with high stone walls, red-tiled roofs, tall cypress trees in the foreground, and an offshore island in the background. Two boats are visible in the calm bay. The printed caption at the top reads "Dubrovnik — Ragusa."

Vintage sepia postcard showing a stone railway viaduct crossing a valley in a hilly, forested landscape, identified as the railway viaduct with the Löbauer Berg. Inset at lower left is a separate view of a tall, ornate iron observation tower rising above trees, labeled as the Friedrich‑August‑Turm. German captions are printed at the top and beside the inset image.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of an old European town with stone fortifications, towers and church buildings in the background, and a narrow lane with trees and small houses in the foreground. Two people in historical dress walk along the street. At the top in red print is a caption in German.

A black‑and‑white image showing a grand neo‑Baroque parliamentary or governmental building with a long façade of tall Corinthian columns, elaborate sculptural groups along the roofline, and two corner towers. A central portico with a pediment and statues is approached by several arched entrances. In front is an open square or broad street with a few pedestrians and a small landscaped garden area. The overall look is that of an early 20th‑century architectural photograph commonly used on postcards.

A vintage black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard composed of many small photographs arranged in a collage. The images show notable sights of Budapest, including monumental buildings, bridges over a river, statues, a parliament‑like building, and park scenes. At the bottom, bilingual greetings in Hungarian and German identify Budapest, along with the publisher's credit.

Vintage sepia-toned street scene showing early 20th‑century downtown Los Angeles. Horse-drawn carriages and pedestrians move along Third Street between multistory commercial buildings. In the distance, the funicular railway known as Angel's Flight is visible climbing the hillside. Red printed captions frame the image, including information about the location and publisher.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a stone arch bridge spanning a rocky gorge with a powerful waterfall or canal outflow beneath it. A group of people in early 20th‑century clothing stand on the bridge, with a horse and cart visible on the left side. Printed caption text appears at the top.

Colorized historic postcard view of a grand neoclassical concert hall with columns and sculptures, fronted by a statue of composer Felix Mendelssohn and formal flowerbeds in a park-like setting. Another ornate institutional building is visible in the background to the right. The sky is clear blue and the overall style suggests an early 20th‑century printed postcard.

Illustrated postcard showing a stylized view of a church with a tall Gothic tower and steep red roofs, fronted by a row of shops and houses. One shop sign reads "ANTON HÄUSLER." The caption at the bottom identifies the scene as the Michaelerkirche in Vienna (Wien).

A colorized panoramic view of a European city with a steep, forested hill dominating the center. On top of the hill stands a fortress-like complex or castle. The city, with red-tiled roofs and several large institutional buildings, spreads around the base of the hill and along a river visible to the right, with bridges and embankments. The style is that of an early 20th‑century printed postcard, with a white border and no visible caption on the image side.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a central square bordered by classical multi‑storey buildings. In the middle stands a large statue on a pedestal surrounded by trees and a fenced area. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk across the open square, and there is a streetlamp in the foreground. The caption at the bottom reads "Graz, Freiheitsplatz."

Vintage sepia postcard showing a cobbled town square with several children and adults standing in the foreground. Surrounding the square are historic multi‑story buildings, and prominently in the background rises a large church with two tall Gothic towers. The left side of the card has open blank space, while the right side contains the town view. Red German text appears at the upper left and along the left margin.

A vintage monochrome postcard showing a canal with a stone bridge in the foreground and a large Gothic-style church with a tall spire and crosses on a rocky hill in the background. Sparse trees and utility poles line the hill. At the top in red print is a short caption in Swedish mentioning the power canal and church in Trollhättan.

Sepia-toned photograph showing a tall stone monument built from rough boulders and dressed masonry. At the top stands a winged female figure (an angel or allegorical Victory) holding up a long cross with a double crossbar. Midway up the plinth there is a niche with a carved cross. Heavy chains hang between stone posts around the base, and trees are visible in the background. No printed caption or handwriting is visible on the front.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a landscaped park with paths, dense shrubbery, and large trees. On the right stands a prominent statue or monument (Julius-Otto-Denkmal). Two women in early 20th‑century clothing walk along the paths. Residential-style buildings are visible in the background. Red printed German text runs along the bottom, including the place name and publisher information.

Colorized panoramic view over a coastal town with red-tiled roofs, fortification walls and bastions projecting into a calm blue bay filled with numerous ships and boats. Hills line the far horizon. In the upper left corner the word "Korfu." is printed, and at the bottom right the web address "www.elia.org.gr" appears.

Vintage black‑and‑white panoramic view of a historic European town seen from the south side, with a foreground of fields and trees. The skyline shows multiple church towers, a large church with a high roof, and fortified towers and walls. Printed text at the bottom identifies the town and viewpoint and credits a publisher from Meissen.

Vintage black-and-white postcard view of a wooden church complex in a rural lakeside landscape. The main church has a steep, hipped roof with a small belfry on top and scaffolding or ladders leaning against the roof, suggesting maintenance work. To the right stands a separate bell tower. In the foreground are fields with haystacks and a wooden fence. Finnish text is printed below the image.

Vintage black-and-white postcard showing a church with multiple spires and a separate wooden bell tower. People in early 20th‑century clothing are gathered outside the church and along the path. Trees frame the scene. The printed caption at the bottom reads "Lerum. Kyrkan." and the publisher's imprint "Jac. Hægerströms förlag." appears at the lower right. There is handwritten vertical text in cursive along the right margin.

An old panoramic black‑and‑white view of a densely built city with many domes and minarets at the foot of a large mountain. The image has a red postage stamp and cancellation mark in the upper right corner, and French captions printed at the bottom. The overall style is that of an early 20th‑century picture postcard.

A black‑and‑white aerial view of a European town with dense, tiled rooftops, several church towers, and a large central building. In the foreground and midground are multi‑storey 19th‑century style townhouses and civic buildings. A church with large Gothic-style windows and another tall tower dominate the skyline. There are visible commercial signs on some buildings. The scene looks out toward open countryside in the far distance. The lower-left corner bears a printed caption and a building sign near the bottom right advertises a local newspaper.

Black-and-white postcard showing a large neoclassical government building with two stories, a central entrance, many windows, and a flag above the main doorway. The building stands in an open square with several trees protected by wooden crates. Printed captions in Portuguese and French at the bottom identify the scene as the Government Palace in the city of Praia, Cabo Verde (Cape Verde).

Sepia-toned vintage postcard view of a wooded hill with buildings and terraces. In the foreground are rooftops and a large bare tree; further up the slope are glasshouse-like structures and pathways. On top of the hill stand fortification-style buildings, and in the background a church tower with a dome and spire rises above the trees. At the top left, printed text reads "Graz. Partie am Schlossberg."

Sepia-toned vertical postcard showing an ornate, Hindu-temple-style palace with a tall tower and intricate carvings, surrounded by a low fence and sandy ground. At the bottom margin, French text reads "HELIOPOLIS - Palais du Baron." There is also a faint round seal and a small website watermark.

Colorized view of a hill covered in greenery with historic buildings. Dominating the right side is a square stone clock tower with large clock faces and a steep, dark roof, known as the Uhrturm. To the left are additional buildings with red-tiled roofs. At the top left of the image, red printed text reads 'Graz. Uhrturm.' The style and coloration suggest an early 20th‑century tourism postcard.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a ceremonial entrance of royals and dignitaries into a large marble stadium packed with spectators. People in formal military uniforms and elegant early‑20th‑century dress walk along the track toward the infield. The architecture suggests a horseshoe‑shaped classical stadium with stone seating rising on both sides and a colonnade at the far end. Printed captions in Greek, French, and English appear along the bottom margin, and a website watermark (elia.org.gr) is visible over the image.

A colorized postcard view of a historic hilltop complex featuring the Albrechtsburg Castle and cathedral towers rising above the town of Meissen on the banks of the Elbe River. In the foreground is the river with a small sailboat; below the castle are clustered houses and riverside buildings with red-tiled roofs. The sky is light blue and the scene has a vintage, hand-tinted look. German captions are printed at the top: on the left identifying the town on the Elbe, and on the right naming the castle and cathedral.

Black‑and‑white panoramic view of a European town with a river in the foreground and dense trees along its banks. A tall round medieval tower with a domed roof stands near a stone gate on a hill, surrounded by historic buildings and sloping streets. Large institutional-looking buildings with mansard roofs dominate the skyline. On the left front, a multi‑storey house bears the sign "Alt‑Heidelberg". The overall scene suggests an early‑20th‑century cityscape.

Tinted vintage postcard view of a round brick chapel with a tall pointed roof, partially framed by trees in a park-like setting. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk or sit on benches along a gravel path in the foreground. Printed captions in Dutch appear below the image, along with a publisher line and some handwritten notes.

Vintage monochrome postcard view of riverside buildings at the foot of a steep, wooded hill with rocky outcrops. On the slope a funicular or electric railway ascends toward fortification structures on the hilltop. The lower margin contains printed German text in red, including the title referencing an electric railway to the Schlossberg and the city name Graz.

Sepia-toned postcard view of a large Gothic-style church with a tall tower rising above a wooded hillside and rooftops. The church dominates the skyline, and in the upper left portion of the card there is printed German text identifying the location and the church, including a note that it was built around the year 1225.

Color postcard showing a panoramic view over a densely built city with many low-rise buildings and a prominent hilltop complex with ancient ruins in the distance. Tall cypress trees frame the foreground. In the upper left corner, red text in Greek and French reads "Άποψις Αθηνών." and "Vue d'Athènes." A web address watermark "www.elia.org.gr" appears at the bottom right.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing an old European street scene with children playing in an open square in front of narrow, multi‑story houses with steep gabled roofs. In the background rises a large church with a steep roof, a clock on its facade, and a small spire. The caption at the bottom reads "Freiberg i. Sa.  Am Mühlgraben."

A black-and-white postcard view across a river toward the baroque skyline of Dresden. The foreground shows a riverside promenade with a balustrade and trees framing the scene. Across the river stand large historic buildings and church towers. The caption at the bottom reads in German: "Dresden  Blick vom Königsufer".

Colorized vintage postcard showing a large statue of a robed clergyman (Mgr. Hamer) on a tall stone pedestal in a landscaped park or square. The base is decorated with numerous wreaths and flowers, and two men in dark clothing and hats stand at the left. Trees and a building appear in the background. At the bottom margin in red print is the caption indicating the city and the statue.

Vintage monochrome (blue-toned) postcard showing a tall medieval tower beside a tree-lined waterway and park, with bridges crossing the water. The printed caption and publisher information appear beneath the image, and there is a handwritten message in cursive on the right side of the card.

A black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a town square bordered by multi‑storey buildings and, in the background, a large fortified complex with high stone walls and a prominent cylindrical tower. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk and stand in the square, and an old car is visible. Mountains rise behind the castle. Caption text is printed along the lower border.

Black‑and‑white view through an old city gate with a large rounded arch opening onto a cobbled street lined with multi‑storey townhouses. Above and to the right of the arch is a baroque‑style niche containing a seated crowned figure in relief, flanked by two standing figures with spears. Several German signs are attached to the wall by the arch. The overall scene suggests a historic European city street photographed in an early 20th‑century style.

Nighttime winter scene of a tall, multi-tiered monument covered in deep snow. A robed figure stands on top of the column-like base, with multiple sculpted figures around the pedestal, all blanketed in snow. Leafless trees and park lights surround the monument, and in the background a warm-lit brick tower with arched windows and a crenellated roof rises above the trees. The sky has a reddish glow typical of city lights on a snowy night. A thin white frame surrounds the image, as is common in printed postcards.

Colorized vintage view over a river running through a European city, with three bridges crossing the water, lined by multi‑story historic buildings with red-tiled roofs. A church tower with an onion-shaped dome stands prominently on the right, and a fortified structure sits on a wooded hill in the background. At the top left, German text reads "Graz mit den 3 Brücken."

A monochrome illustrated postcard showing an old European street scene with steep‑roofed medieval houses and a tall church tower in the background. The drawing is done in pen-and-ink style. At the bottom margin there is a caption in German that reads "REVAL AN DER OLAIKIRCHE."

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing the circular stone ruin known as El Caracol at the Maya archaeological site of Chichén Itzá. The structure rises in tiers of weathered masonry with a partially collapsed upper section under a cloudy sky. Printed caption text in Spanish appears at the bottom of the image.

Colorized historic postcard view of a large gabled town hall building fronting a cobbled square. The building has a steep red roof, a stepped or curved gable with a clock, and a small tower or cupola on top. A fountain or statue stands in front of the facade, and a sign reading "Ratskeller" is visible at street level. People are walking in the square in front of the town hall. The sky is lightly clouded and the overall style suggests an early 20th‑century printed postcard.

Black‑and‑white panoramic view over a historic European city on a wide river. In the foreground are tree‑lined paths and a curving elevated ramp or road leading down the hillside into a dense cluster of 19th‑century buildings with ornate roofs and church towers. On the hill to the left stands a large palace‑like complex. The broad river runs through the center of the image; a prominent suspension bridge with stone towers crosses it, with several steamships and boats on the water. On the far right riverbank a very large, domed neo‑Gothic/neo‑Renaissance parliament‑style building stands prominently. Distant hills form the background. There is no visible printed or handwritten text on the image side.

Vintage sepia stereoscopic image showing two nearly identical photographs side by side of the Parthenon temple ruins on the Acropolis, with rocky foreground and several columns standing. The style is that of an old photographic postcard or stereoview card, with Greek text beneath the image and a modern website watermark overprinted at the bottom.

A black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph showing a wide river with several boats and barges moored along the embankment. On the left side stands a long row of ornate multi‑story 19th‑century buildings with mansard roofs and a central domed structure, forming a classic European riverside boulevard. In the distance on the right is a slender suspension bridge crossing the river. The image is framed by an irregular white vignette border typical of old postcards.

Sepia-toned historical postcard showing a large fortified castle complex surrounded by wooded hills. The main building has steep roofs with many dormer windows and a central tower with turrets. Nearby are ancillary stone and half-timbered buildings, walls, and a pathway leading up from a valley. Printed German text appears at the top left of the image.

Color postcard view of a large medieval clock tower with a steep shingled roof and wooden balcony, standing on a hill overlooking a city. A man in period clothing and hat stands on a path by the tower, looking over the city. Trees and a winding walkway frame the foreground. The printed caption at the top right reads in German.

Colorized historic postcard showing the ornate entrance of a brick Renaissance-style building with stone portal, statues, iron lattice window grilles, green shutters, and steps with railings leading up from a cobbled street. At the bottom edge, a caption in Dutch is printed.

Sepia-toned postcard showing an elevated view of a mosque complex surrounded by trees and low buildings. A prominent square minaret with geometric decoration and a finial stands above tiled roofs. In the foreground, two robed figures stand on a path overlooking the scene. Printed caption at the bottom identifies the location as the Mosque of Sidi Haloui in Tlemcen.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a large Gothic ensemble on a hill above a river, showing a castle-like complex with tall spires and towers (Albrechtsburg Castle and the cathedral) rising above smaller riverside houses. The scene is reflected in the calm water in the foreground. At the bottom, there is a handwritten-style caption in German.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a large Baroque-style palace with a central tower and mansard roof, seen from a formal garden with stairs and trimmed hedges in the foreground. Printed red text at the top identifies the site, and there are red pen marks crossing out a number. The publisher's imprint is printed vertically along the right edge.

Black-and-white postcard view of a church largely hidden behind tall leafy trees and a wooden picket fence. The church has a tall, slender spire rising from a white gabled tower with a circular window. The scene appears tranquil, with a road in the foreground. In the lower-left corner, white text printed on the image identifies the place.

Black‑and‑white view of a busy European city street with tram tracks, pedestrians, shops with awnings, and historic buildings. A large baroque church tower dominates the right side background. Text along the bottom margin identifies the scene as Herrengasse with the city parish church in Graz and notes the publisher and date.

A black‑and‑white panoramic view of a historic European spa town, showing densely packed multi‑story buildings along a valley with a prominent colonnade crowded with people. On the hillside are large villas and grand hotels. The caption at the bottom reads in German: "Weltbad Karlsbad. Blick vom Panorama."

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a large open square with gardens, walking paths, and people strolling. On the left is a long row of multi‑story buildings with arcades and a towered structure in the middle distance. Behind the town rise steep, rocky mountains. The caption at the bottom margin reads "TRENTO - Piazza Venezia," identifying the scene as a city square in Trento, Italy.

Black-and-white postcard showing a canal with a passenger ship named 'JUNO' moored in front of a large Renaissance-style castle with round corner towers and a church-like tower. Trees line both sides of the waterway. The printed caption at the bottom left reads 'Vadstena Slott.' Additional small text with photo credits and numbering appears in the lower right corner.

Black-and-white postcard-style photograph showing a riverside town with a large historic building complex on a wooded hill to the left and a church with a tall tower near the center. Small houses line the riverbank. A paddle steamer crowded with people sails along the river, with another smaller vessel behind it. Trees frame the foreground. In the lower left corner, text reads 'Pirna a.d. Elbe'.

Sepia-toned historic street scene labeled "EISLEBEN Plan" showing a central square with a small pavilion and pond in the foreground, surrounded by multi‑story 19th‑century buildings with shopfronts. People walk across the open square; tram tracks run through it. In the distant background are church towers rising above the town's rooftops. A red handwritten number appears in the upper right corner.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a coastal fortification with round stone walls on a bluff above the sea. A lone figure in traditional dress walks along a grassy path in the foreground. Below the cliff is a shoreline with rocks and small boats or structures in the water, and a town faintly visible in the background. French captions are printed beneath the image.

Black-and-white photograph showing a group of well‑dressed men and women, many wearing suits, hats, and summer dresses, standing on the deck of a boat.
